names.21045: If you stand in the middle of Corpo Plaza and observe what's around you – all the breathtaking megabuildings, office blocks, bars, clubs, architectural wonders and dazzling neon signs – it's hard to believe that only a few decades ago the area looked like a smoldering battlefield in the aftermath of the 4th Corporate War and the nuclear attack on Arasaka Tower. As anyone with a pair of optics can see, City Center was fully rebuilt, surpassing even its former glory with more modern and cutting-edge architecture. It serves one purpose, and one purpose only – to flaunt the city's economic power and prove that Night City is freer than ever before.
names.21048: Heywood is a district of contradictions. The northern part that borders the City Center is modern and well-kept, proud of its stunning megabuildings, parks, and places that are open to the public. But all you have to is go a few blocks southeast and the scenery starts to change dramatically. This part of Heywood is much poorer and more dangerous. The buildings are smaller and the streets are controlled by the Valentinos and the 6th Street Gang. If you know your place and keep your head down, Heywood isn't really so bad. After all, it's where most of Night City sleeps. If you're not a corpo and you score an apartment in the richer part of the district, then you've just won the lottery. Otherwise, just be happy you live in Heywood. In Night City, things could always be worse.
names.21057: Watson was supposed to be the beating heart of Night City. A few decades ago, Japanese zaibatsus invested billions of eurodollars in skyscrapers, nightclubs, the Med Center, even industry in the northern area – all intended to make the district self-sufficient and prosperous. But everything changed when Arasaka returned to the city after the Unification War. The corporation steamrolled all of its competitors, and without a stable financial sector, Watson caved in on itself. Jobs in the Northside Industrial District completely evaporated, leaving people out on the street, allowing Arasaka to buy up all the now-cheap real estate. Turns out, the move was calculated: Arasaka needed port-access. Today Watson is one of Night City's poorest districts, inhabited mainly by workers in Northside earning ennies.
names.21064: You'll find Dakota in an auto repair shop in Rocky Ridge. In Night City, that choice of headquarters might seem strange; out in the middle of nowhere, the garage is nothing short of an oasis. This is where Dakota tugs the strands of her intricate web stretching over the Badlands. If you want to be part of her crew, sooner or later you'll have to pay Rocky Ridge a visit.
names.21070: El Capitan has carved out a nice little place for himself by the beltway in Rancho Coronado with a view onto the dam. It's a secluded place, ideal for making deals that require discretion. If there's something you need to discuss with Capitan in person, he'll probably want to meet you there.
names.21079: If you want to parley with Regina in person, you'll have to head down to Kabuki in Watson. Yaiba, the corporate skyscraper where she's located, is hard to miss – it's mostly surrounded by residential buildings (not to mention Lizzie's Bar, the club of the Mox). Regina conducts biz out of the top floor, which she has reserved all to herself.
names.21086: 7th Hell is a small, seedy nightclub in the heart of the city. While nobody would ever call it their favorite place to be, at a certain point in the night – or at a certain level of intoxication – people just gravitate to the spot. It's that place where that choom of a guy you met in the other bar knows some chick who you gotta meet ... and that's where the night takes you.
names.21128: A former paint factory in Rancho Coronado, Tripple Extreme Gym is now a fight ring belonging to the Animals. Fighters clash in an enormous vat that was once used to mix paints – the postindustrial interior lends the show a unique atmosphere and interesting acoustics.
names.21153: To some a monument to corporate power, to others a symbol of oppression, Arasaka's West Coast headquarters is the heart of the megacorporation's financial and military operations in both Americas. Destroyed in 2023 in a bombing carried out by Johnny Silverhand, the tower later rose from the rubble as a testament to the corporation's ultimate triumph over its enemies. If history's written by the victors, then they made quite sure this particular footnote was written by the hands of the world's best architects. The majestic, 2034-foot steel-and-concrete monolith towers over Corpo Plaza, casting a shadow over every street in Night City – both literally and figuratively. The decisions that fall from the heavily guarded Arasaka Tower determine the lives of all within the city limits.
names.21159: Once a luxury hotel located in the north of Pacifica, now a bustling, repurposed market teeming with goods and information  being traded within the Haitian community. Given the Voodoo Boys' low-key presence in the hotel, it's better not to show up there alone or uninvited.
names.21192: Laguna Bend's evolution has taken it from a quaint, sleepy town, to a suburb of Night City, to a reservoir. Why? Because NC Dam Ltd decided it wanted to build (surprise!) a dam and flooded Laguna Bend and its surroundings before the town's residents could mount any meaningful opposition to it. Water rushed into homes that some people only managed to evacuate on the day of.\n\nGiven what the rest of the Badlands looks like, Laguna Bend is a welcome sight from the outside. Still, it's worth bearing in mind that the water is highly toxic and will most likely remain so for the foreseeable future.
names.21222: The best music store in Night City, maybe even in all of California. Apart from new releases and special deals, you can find real vintage gems procured by the owner, but the closest you'll get to those at first are through the catalog. If you prove yourself enough of a connoisseur, the store owner might give you her inventory of her priceless items and maybe even let you into the veritable music heaven that is the back room. It's no surprise that its location is mostly known by fans, but also artists and famous stars.
names.21225: Besides the two thousand apartments identical to V's, this Watson megablock also features luxury penthouses on its upper floors. Further down, you can find various service points: stores, market stalls, a gym, even a shooting range. To a certain extent, megabuildings are truly self-sufficient, self-contained ecosystems – many of their long-term residents (especially netrunners) haven't stepped outside in years.
names.21229: Bulwark is a shopping center situated right on the Wellsprings waterfront. There, you can find good quality implants as well as bars and eateries to suit any palate. The clean, well-maintained Bulwark is also a great place for a walk, even if you don't plan on grabbing some new chrome.
names.21232: A shady, scavenger-run marketplace in Northside. The vendors set up their wares in old, repurposed transport containers, and most of what they offer's been smuggled in.
names.21250: A multimillion-eurodollar undertaking, an industrial feat, two million hectoliters of toxic water and hundreds of flooded homes. Welcome to the Badlands.\n\nWhen the dam was under construction, it was obvious there would also be a reservoir – which sounded great in theory. The townsfolk put that piece of knowledge in the back of their heads and didn't stop to wonder why they needed a dam, why here of all places, and who was profiting from it. Spoiler alert: it wasn't the town's residents, and since losers don't get to write history, any memory of them and their tragedy evaporated from the collective consciousness as quickly as the morning dew on a hot summer's morning.
names.21256: A shopping mall between Corpo Plaza and the Glen offering lovely views of the nearby park and port. If you have the eddies for top-shelf tech, weapons, clothes and restaurants, then the View is the place for you. Find everything you need under one roof, all draped in luxury and tasteful elegance.

names.86279: A pavilion in Terra Cognita technology park dedicated to extraplanetary travel. The exhibit offered a range of information, tips and anecdotes that might be useful to would-be travelers as well as lectures about this ever-evolving industry. Many educational activities were geared toward younger people, including the opportunity to talk with recruiters from corporations involved in aerospace technology, engineering and exploration.\n\nToday, all that remains of the exhibit is a lone shuttle. Most everything else has been stripped for salvage and sold off by Dogtown's inhabitants.
names.86281: An abandoned pavilion in the Terra Cognita technology park dedicated to nature, consisting of several multilevel greenhouses. The exhibits here showcased large specimens of non-indigenous flora cultivated in artificial microclimates as well as several reptile species on the verge of extinction. The real crowdpleaser, however, would be the dinosaur skeletons with holographic reconstructions of tissue projected directly onto the fossilized bones. Over the years, this technologically ambitious enerprise and time capsule for nature's splendor has become overgrown with vegetation... All the more reason to visit, perhaps?
names.86283: The Scraper is what remains of one of the last investments before the district's closure. This immense structure, located far from the skyline of City Center, was supposed to offer a relaxing, yet luxurious getaway for Night City's rich – though, not necessarily the filthy rich. According to an investor's brochure, the Scraper was designed to be a "modern, 4-star hotel complex located on the picturesque Pacific coast, offering over 250 suites with breathtaking vistas and fitted with the latest in stylish amenities." Of course, those plans clearly failed to materialize.\n\nToday, scavengers have moved in and brought their own decor with them. Stolen tech and cyberware have replaced chic coffee tables. And in place of plush loveseats, they've installed cozy cages for their long-stay "guests".
names.86285: The Nighthawks Rehabilitation Center was intended to serve the players of the city's dream football team – their health, fitness and (perhaps most importantly) the condition of their advanced cyberware. Investors spared no expense on state-of-the-art equipment for "groundbreaking" (translates to: highly illegal) surgeries. They also hired a staff of biomedical specialists, from ripperdocs and sports physiologists, to sleep specialists, nutrition strategists and acupuncture experts.\n\nThe whole investment quickly fell through, however. The Nighthawks only managed to play only a few games before the team was dissolved, along with any hope of revitalizing Pacifica. It wasn't until the district came under Kurt Hansen's rule that the lights at the former Rehabilitation Center turned back on and stayed on. Perhaps, there's a certain irony here – the place where people were supposed to heal is now a factory for instruments of death, both for BARGHEST itself and for outside buyers. One thing, however, has not changed – no one here fears the law.
names.86287:
The Holy Haven Catholic Church was built with donations from the pockets of Night City's wealthy Catholics at a time when South Pacifica was set to once again become home to the city's affluent. Although the church construction was completed, an exodus of investors buried any hope of repopulating the neighborhood.

It wasn't until Kurt Hansen seized control of Dogtown that the church's pews began to fill. Down-on-their-luck outlaws prayed here for a better tomorrow and sought forgiveness for the sins that had forced them to seek refuge behind Dogtown's walls. But when a better tomorrow never came, and new sins erased memories of the old, the ranks of the faithful began to wither.

The parish's most recent pastor, Odell Blanco, helped repurpose the church building to house a clinic for the area's neediest, which he runs together with ripperdoc and physician Anthony Anderson. Although the scope and quality of medical care here leave much to be desired, Haven Clinic remains the only hope for many of Dogtown's destitute. As Odell might say, "When you have nothing, everything is a gift."
names.86290:
Halsey, Ferris & Skiv began the construction of this colossus in 2061, intending to erect Night City's most impressive hotel to date. However, along with the rest of Pacifica's redevelopment, the project took a fatal nosedive. Following the end of the Unification War, Kurt Hansen laid claim to the half-finished hotel as his new base of operations. Today, the Black Sapphire serves as the shining star around which all of Dogtown revolves.

It stands ninety-nine stories tall with a luxury club, casino and AV landing pads at the top. The ground floor contains warehouses and barracks for BARGHEST soldiers. Everything in between remains a matter of speculation - a prison for VIPs held for ransom, a zoo for endangered animals that Hansen serves to dinner guests at lavish parties, a server room that puts Arasaka Tower's to shame...

It's no surprise the rumors that circle the Black Sapphire grow more and more farfetched every year. Yet one fact is undeniable – the Black Sapphire is Hansen's pride and joy. It is an impenetrable fortress, a palace where he can play King of Dogtown and host dignitaries from the world over, but especially the who's who of Night City's political and criminal landscape.
names.86292: Officially, very little is known about Project Cynosure. Unofficially? Even less. Putting together the scraps of available information, flimsy hypotheses and conspiracy theories, Project "Cynosure" appears to be Militech's prematurely terminated, secret military research project.\n"Project Cynosure" was Militech's attempt in the second decade of the 21st century to develop an experimental weapon, or tool, to support Militech netrunners venturing into the deepest regions of cyberspace to capture and tame so-called "rogue AIs." These AIs were then to be used in a secret facility located somewhere beneath Pacifica. To what end? Most likely to enhance Militech's military and intelligence capabilities, or perhaps for something even more serious: a competitor to Soulkiller, Arasaka's flagship cyber-weapon.\nHad Militech succeeded, it is likely that the geopolitical landscape in the region, and perhaps the entire world, would look very different. Yet for reasons unknown, the creation of the anti-Soulkiller never happened. According to rumors, Project Cynosure was canceled and buried. Some speculate that a series of accidents occurred in the project's laboratories. Others that the Militech-captured AIs broke free from their shackles and took control of the facility. Still other theories suggest that Arasaka or the cyberspace watchdog, NetWatch, caught wind of the project's existence, forcing Militech to cover its tracks to avoid a diplomatic crisis or even war. What's certain is that the truth will likely never be known.
names.86294: The nation's top military medical complex, named after a former NUS Air Force surgeon-in-chief. Situated in the verdant serenity of a park in Langley, not far from FIA headquarters, it has served NUS presidents and other esteemed officials for many years. The center's state-of-the-art equipment, team of accomplished doctors and its peaceful environs all play a role in its reputation for elite care and the quick recovery time of its patients.
names.86296:
A huge, neon pyramid in the heart of Dogtown. The Heavy Hearts Club was supposed to be a postcard highlight for a revitalized Pacifica, but now it plays home to the largest nightclub in Kurt Hansen's domain. The deals with the highest stakes are struck under Hansen's watchful eye in the Black Sapphire or the stadium. Everything else is settled here.

The Heavy Hearts has established itself as the go-to meeting place where important players can discuss side deals during their stay in Dogtown. Maybe you ordered a dozen tanks from Hansen at the stadium, but you'd like to land a ultra-rare Rayfield before leaving Night City. Maybe you're in town to have Kurt smuggle a dozen crates of assault rifles into Myanmar, but there's also a shipment of contraband Zetatech cyberware burning a hole in your pocket. In such cases, be sure to make a stop at the Heavy Hearts before going on your merry way.

Of course, maybe you're not a corpo, politician or dirty cop looking to make a deal at all. Maybe you just want to dance the night away without worry of waking up dead in a ditch the next morning. The Heavy Hearts Club has it all.
names.86298:
Night City International and Translunar Spaceport (NCX) is Orbital Air's flagship investment in North America. It was built between 2045 and 2047 where the majestic Morro Rock volcanic neck, a geological feature sacred to local Native American tribes, had stood for 23 million years. But it wasn't heartless corpos who gave permission to demolish the rock – Night City authorities did.

In consultation with a group of investors, the Mayor of Night City agreed to sign a contract to construct a mass driver at the site. Orbital Air management was understandably skeptical that rocket-free launches could successfully take place without corporate backing to ensure its profitability. Therefore, the aerospace megacorp proposed buying up the surrounding land and sprearheading further investment, offering to build a civilian spaceport in the process.

Orbital Air only partially fulfilled the deal, however. By taking advantage of several legal loopholes, the corp cancelled a provision in the arrangement for completing the mass driver's construction. Its rusted, incomplete remains were then eventually dismantled, and OA's monopoly on space colonization remained intact.

Night City International and Translunar Spaceport handles more than 100 million passengers a year and contains three terminals. Terminal A is home to OA TerraLines, a relatively low-cost airline that provides low-orbit transportation services around the globe. Terminal B houses the slightly more expensive OA Tycho and Crystal Palace Direct lines, hauling travelers to the largest lunar city and the famous space station, respectively. Terminal C, on the other hand, is where OA Black and OA HighLines luxury shuttles operate. The purpose and destinations of these flights remain largely unknown, and the cost of that discretion is reflected in the exorbitant ticket prices.
names.86300:
In the heart of Longshore Stacks you'll find a safe haven for any seeking to quench their thirst with a glass of the good stuff and a place to relax with some classic jukebox tunes. Regulars know that the owner and bartender of this establishment are one and the same person. Seven years ago, the woman they know as Daphne laid claim to this vacant building sitting atop an out-of-service boiler room and transformed it into a godsend for the Stacks community – a bar.

To this day, Stacks residents relish visiting the Moth after a rough day, where they're always greeted by a bartender bot or by the owner herself. Daphne's ears are always open to the locals' ramblings and ravings. She has her finger on the pulse of all Dogtown gossip. In fact, if Daphne finds your gossip juicy as all git-out, she might just offer you a round on the house.

In other words, if you're an ennyless Dogtown resident without proper access to a therapist, then you head to Moth, order a stiff drink and talk your heart out to Daphne. It should come as no surprise that this bar never lacks clientele.
names.86302: Once home to the Night City Nighthawks football team, EBM Petrochem Stadium now hosts a bustling hub for illegal trade. The black market within caters not only to the residents of Dogtown, but also to many of Night City's largest corprorations and most influential players – off the books, of course.\n\nA nuclear-powered aerozep that crashed into the field once upon a time now serves as the primary power source for entire stadium as well as several surrounding buildings.
names.86303: A residential quarter of Dogtown packed densely with makeshift structures fashioned from shipping containers, old construction equipment and debris. A city within a city that offers everything the average Dogtown resident needs: trade, bars, a central plaza, and even a hotel. Much of the new tech flowing into Hansen's market at the stadium first has its serial numbers filed off here. If you're searching for a missing person, this is the place to start. If all you want is a warm scopburger and a cold beer, go no farther than the Stacks.\n\nKids chase each other in a maze of sheet metal. A local boozehound musician picks at guitar strings. A junkie rubs one out to a skin BD in the comfort of his rusty cargo container. Life finds a way.
names.86306:
In the 2020s Militech established a secret, experimental military project in this part of Pacifica, constructing bunkers and laboratories cleverly hidden beneath urban infrastructure. Nearly half a century later, a group of investors appeared, unaware they were building on the remains of an old military complex. When a lab was excavated at one of the construction sites, the investors were forced out of Pacifica and Militech erected a wall around the neighborhood ostensibly due to gas leaks, poor documentation on local developments and unexploded ordnance from the 4th Corporate War.

In 2077, Dogtown has become a kind of city within a city, walled off from the rest of Night with designated points of entry manned by Kurt Hansen's Militech-commandos-turned-militia-soldiers. On the streets one can still see the remnants of Pacifica's never-completed redevelopment - luxury hotels, swimming pools, dazzlingly sumptuous mansions: once destined for glory, now a dilapadated mess. Machinery abandoned by construction workers is also present and many of the buildings are nothing more than crumbling, vacant husks.

The NCPD is forbidden to enter Dogtown proper, while Trauma Team rarely ventures inside due to the increased risk and the fact that hardly anyone in Dogtown has TT insurance. True enough, Hansen's people serve as local law enforcement, but are far from what one would call "police officers". Maybe they'll help, maybe they won't - their primary concern is ensuring the neighborhood doesn't descend into total anarchy. Small local squabbles and conflicts? Not worth their precious time.

So who lives in Dogtown? Mostly those on the run from corps, gangs or the NCPD. But ordinary people find themselves in the mix too - those pushed beyond the margins of society in Night City and who were brave or desperate enough to try their luck here.

names.87611: The stadium is the beating heart of Dogtown, and the Tunnel is one of its main arteries. This is where BARGHEST smuggles illegal weapons and tech into Night City.\n\nImagine you're a corp CEO – you need to equip a gang to do some dirty work for you, and you need it done quietly. You go to the stadium in Dogtown, choose a supplier, pay up front, then let Hansen's people take care of the rest. Within 48 hours, 6th Street will have their hands on those sixty Militech M251s Ajax rifles you ordered.
names.87613: One of the most distinctive examples of Brutalist architecture in the never-quite-finished district of Pacifica. Today it is an important landmark for Dogtown residents and serves as a den for a local cluster of Voodoo Boys. It is here that illegal programs, daemons and hacks are made then sent of to be sold under the counter in Kabuki. This is where the real tech wizards weave their magic. Overclocked decks, processors with stripped-down safety features, bootleg drivers – these things and more are made in batches by Slider and his crew. There's a strong chance that the hacks bought and sold in the netrunner networks of the Kabuki Roundabout were born right here in the heart of Luxor Heights within the concrete skeleton of Eventide Resort & Spa.
names.87615:
The NCPD exists to serve and protect one thing – statistics. The fewer the murders and assaults, the higher their praise from the mayor. The higher the praise, the fatter their bonuses.

NCPD officers like to close the book on most cases as quickly as possible. They come across a dead body in a dark alley with multiple gunshot wounds to the head and torso, they call it a suicide. People die violent deaths in Night City every day, but rarely will the police classify these as "murder".

The statistics at the NCPD station in Pacifica painted too grim (read: realistic) a picture, so the city shuttered it overnight. Today, the station serves those who never made it into official police statistics, but who are certainly more than deserving.
names.87620: The avant-garde exterior of Luxor High Wellness Spa brings to mind the monumental feats of the ancient world such as the now-demolished Temple of Hatshepsut and the mysterious ziggurats of Mesopotamia. It was designed by prominent architect Dionizy Haponik (born 09-11-2021 in Warsaw, Poland) who was known to draw heavy inspiration from sacral architecture.\n\nUnfinished since the 2050s, the building was to become a modern temple for beauty and spiritual bliss, where wealthy Pacifica residents and visitors could indulge in expensive rituals to prolong their lives. Never mind the fact their synthetic skin, titanium bones and genetically boosted metabolisms were already doing a solid job of that. This place was designed to be the very definition of luxury – prohibitively expensive and wholly unnecessary.
names.87621: The Center for Neuromotor Development Site 341 is a cutting-edge facility dedicated to the development of young athletes. Its main goal is to discover young talent and shepherd them into successful careers. Prospective athletes spend years under the guidance of specialists – ripperdocs, coaches, biohackers and psychologists. These young athletes undergo genetic and cybernetic modification to ensure their nervous systems are capable of high performance from an early age.\n\nHowever, not all bodies can withstand the demands of modern-day competitive sports, whose spectacle lies partially in taking risks and pushing the limits of human capability. As the "341" in its name would imply, there are hundreds of such facilities across the world. Not all operate in accordance with the law.
names.87625:
Rumor has it that Militech bought as many bottles of champagne for the this exhibition's opening as there were liters of concrete already poured into the district's construction. The unending flow of bubbly, the self-aggrandizing applause and the lofty promises delivered during the ceremony were intended to inflate egos and encourage the city's elite to open their wallets for the next stages of development. The guest list included everyone who wielded influence in the city and the bank account to back it up.

Alas, although the grand opening was meant to last a couple of days, it never came to pass. This exhibit-turned-mausoleum of grand ideas and ambitions continues to rot in Dogtown to this day, a mockery and reminder of the past's utopian plans for the future. Nothing remains of the weapon displays and special security systems. Everything that wasn't nailed to the floor (and even the things that were) have long since been removed and are likely repurposed in such mundane ways it would cause the expo's original designers to shed a tear.

Today, Colonel Hansen and his comrades like to receive prominent guests here. After all, what better way to kick off an potential business venture than by spinning a tale of abandoned citizens taking the future into their own hands.
names.87626: A temple for technology located in the Terra Cognita technology park that was built to showcase the latest innovations produced by the world's leading tech manufacturers. The exhibits here were designed to be an interactive, hands-on experience to raise awareness for cyberware's potential as well as boost healthy competition between producers.\n\nToday, the pavilion is infested with scavs who tirelessly pick apart the exhibit, like vultures on a carcass, as part of their illegal trade of cybernetic components.

names.90915:
Tycho was founded in 1997 by the European Space Council. The Moon was chosen as the site for the first human settlement in space for obvious reasons: the presence of natural gravity and the relative softness of the ground. The city is located at the bottom of an awe-inspiring impact crater bearing the same name that measures 53 miles wide and nearly 3 miles deep.

By 2020, most of Tycho's structures had been moved underground. A network of caves and tunnels was hollowed out with atomic laser drills, and the ceilings were reinforced with molten lunar sand. Within the cave system, settlers created reserves of oxygen-producing plant life that accounts for most of breathable air in the community today.

According to data from 2075, Tycho boasts a population of approximately 40,000, and is the largest of two populated settlements (the other being Copernicus with a population of approximately 18,000 people). The transportation of raw materials from Tycho to Earth and to the nearby Crystal Palace space station is done via mass drivers. Two of these drivers are located in Tycho, the other at Copernicus. During the so-called First Orbital War in 2008, which lasted six hours, a 2-ton moonstone launched from a Tycho mass driver struck Colorado Springs. Most of the commanding officers of the NUS armed forces perished in the explosion, bringing an abrupt end to the conflict.

names.97808:
Night Corp Tower stands at the heart of City Center – the headquarters of one of the city’s oldest and most enigmatic corporations. Officially dedicated to civic renewal, the Tower serves both as a monument to Night City’s founder and as a nerve center for the future of the metropolis’s public infrastructure.

While City Hall oversees municipal works and administrative affairs, Night Corp’s ambitions extend further – into the study of societal dynamics, behavioral engineering and sociotechnical control. Behind its fortress-like façade, thousands of engineers, analysts and administrators pursue projects aimed at reshaping the next evolution of society.

Ever since the rebuilding of downtown, the corporation’s inner workings have remained shrouded in secrecy. Employees operate in strict isolation, biometric access separating teams by floor to prevent cross-contamination of data. Building schematics have never been made public, fueling persistent rumors of a vast subterranean datacenter – an unseen project said to utilize experimental AI that tracks Night Citizens and models their possible futures. An unconfirmed theory, but one that fits the pattern.

The tower is both a beacon and a black box – built to guide the city's future, though leaving many questions unanswered.
names.97813:
Erected at the foot of Arasaka Tower, the Arasaka Memorial honors the victims of the 2023 AHQ Disaster. Built partly from the preserved ruins of the original structure, it ventures past remembrance and into immersion.

A cold, foreboding hush often settles over visitors when they cross the suspended glass walkway overlooking the shattered lobby, and likewise when they stand under the red-tinted lights meant to mimic the sky's hue in the moments following the blast. In these spaces, the air weighs heavy with memories of radioactive ash and unspeakable pain. Visitors say it’s easier to imagine themselves standing amidst the choking dust and scattered blazes of that fateful night.

Outside, it’s common to see Buddhist monks keeping an eternal vigil lit. Further in, the courtyard contains a tiered columbarium – rows of dark monoliths that represent the countless lives lost in a single act of terror.

Whether regarded as a sincere tribute or as a carefully curated act of image control, this memorial endures as one of Night City’s most haunting landmarks – a place where grief and corporate legacy share the same stone.

names.98608:
Located in Arroyo, Santo Domingo, Night City Prison serves as the NCPD’s primary maximum-security penitentiary, housing many of the city’s most violent offenders. Under the uncompromising leadership of Warden Momma Warsaw, the facility has earned a dark reputation for its oppressive atmosphere and authoritarian belief that fear succeeds where rehabilitation fails. For anyone inside these walls, inmate or visitor, every movement is scrutinized and every infraction carries consequences.

One of the prison’s most controversial practices is braindance therapy, a type of rehabilitation that forces inmates to relive simulations of violence, loss, and death inspired by the crimes they committed. Although intended to evoke genuine empathy, guilt and regret, the program has shown a tendency to leave inmates psychologically shattered rather than rehabilitated. It is considered the primary cause of the prison riot of 2077.

During a facility-wide blackout, Arturo, a civilian braindance tech, altered the prison’s braindance experiences to show peaceful memories and idealized lives. This unexpected change proved catastrophic. Thirteen inmates took their own lives, unable to cope with these glimpses of freedoms they would never know again. Those suicides triggered a days-long riot that claimed the lives of dozens of inmates and multiple prison guards.

In the riot’s aftermath, Warsaw authorized sweeping security reforms. The most dangerous inmates were implanted with new Reaper Compliance Chips, allowing guards to remotely execute violent offenders and instigators before chaos could spread. Maximum Security blocks were restructured to isolate high-risk prisoners, cooperation with MaxTac was expanded, and braindance rehabilitation programs were intensified. Even in Night City, there are few places where hope dies faster than inside the walls of Night City Prison.
